claims.statement: For a Boolean gate split on selector bias s, W=(1-s)W0+sW1+s(1-s)[d-(q1-q0)^2].
Under full-support product bias, W=0 iff the gate is constant or a literal/negated literal.
If W<=epsilon and s in [alpha,1-alpha], then min(d,1-d)<=2epsilon/[alpha(1-alpha)]; in the d near 1 branch, 1-|q1-q0|<=3epsilon/[alpha(1-alpha)].
For XOR with fixed first bias p and selector bias s->0, W=s(1-s)V_p while d-(q1-q0)^2=V_p stays positive; the exact quotient is -[Gamma(p)+Gamma(s)-Gamma(p+s-2ps)]/[s(1-s)V_p].
For W>0, adding c*u(1-u) to Gamma translates the gate-margin quotient -D/W by exactly -c; at W=0 no division is made.
Uniformly control the shaped/replacement-potential gate-margin quotient in bias-boundary contractions after reducing to the live child, retaining child defects and selector entropy terms.
